france24fr.description: Un chef présumé de l'organisation criminelle DZ Mafia, Mehdi Laribi, a été interpellé en Algérie fin juillet sur exécution d'un mandat d'arrêt de la justice française dont il était "une cible prioritaire", selon le ministre de la Justice Gérald Darmanin.

france24fr.title: Israël dit ne pas accepter le plan pour Gaza soutenu par les États-Unis
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre israélien, Benjamin Netanyahu, a affirmé qu'Israël n'avait pas accepté un plan pour Gaza soutenu par les Etats-Unis, même après avoir reçu l'assurance qu'un retrait israélien du territoire palestinien n'interviendrait qu'après le désarmement complet du Hamas.

france24fr.title: 🔴 États-Unis : Abdul El-Sayed, visage de la nouvelle gauche, remporte la primaire démocrate dans le Michigan
Guinée : l'Association des blogueurs dénonce des restrictions de l'accès à Internet
france24fr.description: En Guinée, l'accès à Internet reste fortement perturbé. Facebook, YouTube et TikTok demeurent inaccessibles sans VPN. L'Association des blogueurs de Guinée dénonce une restriction de la liberté d'expression et met en cause les autorités.

france24fr.title: L'ère des machines humanoïdes : la Silicon Valley veut mettre des robots dans notre quotidien
france24fr.description: Longtemps cantonnés à la science-fiction, les robots humanoïdes sont désormais l'un des secteurs les plus convoités de la Silicon Valley. Selon le cabinet McKinsey, l'automatisation pourrait transformer d'ici 2030 jusqu'à 30 % des heures travaillées aujourd'hui dans l'économie américaine. Des dizaines d'entreprises développent déjà des robots capables d'interagir avec les humains, voire de les assister dans certaines tâches du quotidien. Reportage de Pierrick Leurent et Valérie Defert.

france24fr.title: Le président de la Fifa, Gianni Infantino, tient une réunion de crise au Maroc
france24fr.description: Le président de la Fifa Gianni Infantino, assailli de critiques après un projet finalement avorté d'ouverture de l'instance mondiale aux investisseurs privés, tient mercredi au Maroc une réunion de crise avec de hauts responsables de l'organisation.

france24fr.title: Primaire démocrate au Michigan : un coude à coude représentatif des fractures du parti
france24fr.description: Les démocrates du Michigan ont choisi mardi leur candidat au Sénat entre la modérée Haley Stevens, soutenue par l’establishment, et le progressiste Abdul El‑Sayed, appuyé par Bernie Sanders. Les résultats se font encore attendre. Le vainqueur affrontera en novembre le républicain Mike Rogers, dans une course clé pour la reconquête de la majorité sénatoriale.

france24fr.title: À Ceuta, les exilés subsahariens dans l'impasse
france24fr.description: Des exilés d'Afrique subsaharienne ont profité de l'afflux massif de migrants vers Ceuta la semaine dernière pour entrer dans l'enclave espagnole. Contrairement aux migrants marocains renvoyés dans leur pays, ils n'ont, pour l'heure, pas été expulsés. Ils ont été regroupés sur la plage de Trampolín, au nord de l'enclave, et disent souffrir de la faim.

france24fr.title: Allemagne : un drone avec explosif perturbe l'aéroport de Leipzig, hub stratégique pour l'Ukraine
france24fr.description: Le trafic aérien à l'aéroport de Leipzig, dans l'est de l'Allemagne, a été temporairement interrompu dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi après la découverte d'un drone transportant un "engin explosif non identifié". "Un deuxième objet volant non identifié aurait percuté un avion-cargo" en vol, ont par ailleurs indiqué mercredi les enquêteurs allemands.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : Kiev sous les missiles russes, les défenses aériennes submergées
france24fr.description: Au moins 17 personnes ont été tuées dans une nouvelle attaque russe contre Kiev et sa région. Malgré l'interception de nombreux drones, l'Ukraine affirme n'avoir abattu aucun des missiles balistiques tirés par la Russie, faute de suffisamment d'intercepteurs pour ses systèmes Patriot.

france24fr.title: Un étage d'une fusée SpaceX s'est écrasé sur la Lune : quelle opportunité scientifique ?
france24fr.description: L’étage supérieur de la fusée Falcon-9 de SpaceX s’est écrasé sur la Lune ce mercredi matin. Conséquence d’un changement de trajectoire inattendu, la collision va laisser un cratère à la surface lunaire. L’impact est sans danger pour la Terre, assure la NASA. Décryptage avec notre grand reporter, James André.

france24fr.title: Primaire démocrate dans le Michigan : qui sera élu entre Haley Stevens et Abdul El‑Sayed ?
france24fr.description: Les démocrates du Michigan ont choisi mardi leur candidat au Sénat entre la modérée Haley Stevens, soutenue par l’establishment, et le progressiste Abdul El‑Sayed, appuyé par Bernie Sanders. Les résultats se font encore attendre. Le vainqueur affrontera en novembre le républicain Mike Rogers, dans une course clé pour la reconquête de la majorité sénatoriale.

france24fr.title: Le géant russe d'e-commerce, Wildberries, accusé par Kiev d'approvisionner l'armée russe
france24fr.description: Quinze installations logistiques appartenant à Wildberries ont été attaquées en Russie au cours des dix-huit derniers jours, a affirmé le commandant ukrainien Robert Brovdi. Plusieurs attaques d’entrepôts ont eu lieu dans la nuit de lundi à mardi.

france24fr.title: CAC 40 : pourquoi la Bourse de Paris bat des records malgré les crises
france24fr.description: Le CAC 40 a signé un nouveau record historique en clôture mardi, cinq mois après son précédent sommet. Une performance qui peut surprendre alors que la dette française atteint des niveaux record, que les tensions géopolitiques restent fortes et que l'économie mondiale demeure sous pression. Un paradoxe qui s'explique d'abord par les résultats des grandes multinationales.

france24fr.title: Crise à la Fifa : fragilisé, Gianni Infantino tient une réunion au Maroc
france24fr.description: Sous le feu des critiques après son projet finalement abandonné d'ouvrir la Fifa aux investisseurs privés, Gianni Infantino réunit plusieurs hauts responsables de l'instance au Maroc mercredi. Les raisons du choix du royaume, qui coorganisera le Mondial 2030, restent inconnues.

france24fr.title: En Libye, indignation après la vidéo d'une femme flagellée publiquement pour adultère
france24fr.description: Une rare vidéo prise ce 21 juillet à Sebha, en Libye, montre une femme accusée d'adultère condamnée à 100 coups de fouet. Partagée sur les réseaux sociaux, elle suscite l'indignation pour différentes raisons : certains sont outrés par l'application de la peine dans un lieu public, d'autres par l'existence même de la loi sur les relations en dehors d'un mariage.

nzz.description: Banken wie die UBS erwarten weitere Kursgewinne. Treiber der Euphorie ist ein starkes Gewinnwachstum. Der Aufschwung erfasst zunehmend auch europäische Aktien.

spiegel.description: Kaum zurückgetreten, ermittelt die ukrainische Justiz gegen Olha Stefanischyna. Bis vor wenigen Tagen war sie Botschafterin ihres Landes in den USA. Laut Medienberichten wird ihr unrechtmäßige Bereicherung vorgeworfen.

spiegel.title: ORF-III-Chef Peter Schöber abberufen und beurlaubt
spiegel.description: Immer wieder kam es in den vergangenen Jahren im ORF zu Skandalen. Nun ist ORF-III-Generaldirektor Peter Schöber beurlaubt worden. Dessen Verhalten sei mit dem einer Führungskraft »nicht vereinbar«.

spiegel.title: Reem Alabali Radovan: »Ich bin selbst als Flüchtlingskind nach Deutschland gekommen«
spiegel.description: Reem Alabali Radovan ist Ministerin für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung. Sophia und Carl, beide 10, hat sie erzählt, wie ihr Ministerium Kindern auf der ganzen Welt helfen will.

spiegel.title: TikTok: Nutzer dürfen Filmausschnitte von Disney nutzen
spiegel.description: Auf Social Media dürfen Nutzer in den USA bald Ausschnitte aus Disneyfilmen zeigen. TikToker können Sequenzen aus Marvel, Star Wars und Co. benutzen. Im Gegenzug hat Disney auch Anspruch auf ihre Kurzvideos.

spiegel.title: Debatte über Christopher Nolans »Odyssee«: »Das hat mit Homer nichts zu tun«
spiegel.description: Christopher Nolans »Odyssee« steht in der Kritik. Der Althistoriker Raimund Schulz hat mit der Hollywoodvariante kein Problem – und erklärt, wovon der Mythos wirklich handelt.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: Ebola verbreitet sich in DR Kongo laut Ärzte ohne Grenzen in »beispiellosem Tempo«
spiegel.description: Mehr als 1700 Menschen sind nach offiziellen Zahlen mittlerweile durch die Ebolaepidemie in der DR Kongo ums Leben gekommen. Beobachter sehen keine Anzeichen, dass der Ausbruch sich verlangsamt.

spiegel.title: Dinosaurier: Darum gab es keine sehr kleinen Arten
spiegel.description: Manche waren gewaltig, andere nur so groß wie ein Fuchs – aber kein Dinosaurier blieb klein wie eine Maus. Forscher haben einen Verdacht, warum es keine Miniatur-Dinos gab.

spiegel.title: London – Covent Garden: Frau soll auf mehrere Männer eingestochen haben
spiegel.description: Vier Männer sind laut der Londoner Polizei mit Stichverletzungen im Krankenhaus, eine Frau in Gewahrsam. Nach einem Angriff im Bezirk Covent Garden ist die Lage noch unübersichtlich.

spiegel.title: Thomas Bareiß: CDU-Abgeordneter kündigt nach Autounfall Auszeit an
spiegel.description: Thomas Bareiß hat einen schweren Unfall gehabt. Bei einer Blutanalyse stellte sich heraus: Er hatte wohl synthetische Betäubungsmittel konsumiert. Nun bittet der CDU-Politiker in einer Erklärung um Entschuldigung.

spiegel.title: Pinkeln: Treibt Bier mehr als andere Getränke?
spiegel.description: Von Bier muss man besonders häufig pinkeln, heißt es. Ein Ernährungswissenschaftler sagt, was dran ist und ob es einen Unterschied gibt zwischen Getränken mit und ohne Alkohol.

spiegel.title: Russland: Chef von Drohnen-Hersteller bei Autoexplosion schwer verletzt
spiegel.description: Wladimir Tkatschuk soll sich in einem kritischen Zustand befinden: Der Wagen des Chefs von Uraldronsawod ist laut übereinstimmenden Medienberichten explodiert. Die Behörden ermitteln wegen versuchten Mordes.

spiegel.title: Flughafen Leipzig/Halle: Roboter im Einsatz gegen Sprengstoff-Drohne
spiegel.description: Nach dem verdächtigen Drohnenfund am Leipziger Flughafen rückte die Polizei mit Spezialgerät an.

spiegel.title: Russland - Ukraine: Milliarden-Erträge aus eingefrorenen russischen Vermögen für Ukraine
spiegel.description: Seit der Vollinvasion der Ukraine verhängt die EU Sanktionen gegen das Russland von Kremlchef Wladimir Putin. Gelder wurden festgesetzt, die Erträge aus den Zinsen sollen jetzt Kyjiw zugutekommen.

spiegel.title: AfD – Rott am Inn: Ermittlungen gegen Michael Maurer wegen falscher Verdächtigung
spiegel.description: Michael Maurer wollte Bürgermeister von Rott am Inn werden. Der AfD-Politiker erlangte Bekanntheit durch einen Vorfall an einem Wählerstand. Einen vermeintlichen Angriff von Linken hat es aber gar nicht gegeben.

spiegel.title: Gianni Infantino: Luís Figo wirft Fifa-Präsident Niedertracht, Betrug und Feigheit vor
spiegel.description: Der frühere Weltfußballer Luís Figo ätzt gegen Gianni Infantino. In einem Gastbeitrag schreibt er, für die Wahrung der Würde des Fifa-Präsidenten sei es zu spät – für die Rettung des Fußballs nicht.

spiegel.title: Ölkonzerne erzielen zwischen Iran-Krieg und Hitzewellen 93 Milliarden Dollar Gewinn
spiegel.description: Acht der größten Ölkonzerne haben ihre Gewinne im Frühjahresquartal im Vergleich zum Vorjahr fast verdoppelt. Die neuen Zahlen heizen die Debatte über eine Übergewinnsteuer an.

observador.title: Guerra do futuro: tecnologia barata vence meios caros?
observador.description: Azeredo Lopes considera que a Ucrânia atingiu um novo patamar de eficácia com meios baratos. Sublinha que a NATO está obsoleta e os EUA têm estoques baixos devido ao uso de armas caras contra drones.

observador.title: Óculos para eclipse solar esgotam de novo
observador.description: O stock foi reforçado na terça-feira, mas voltou a esgotar esta quarta. Quem não conseguir pode comprar óculos certificados por cerca de 3€ em farmácias e supermercados.

observador.title: Putin responde a Ucrânia e cria unidade de drones
observador.description: Em resposta à Ucrânia, Putin nomeou Denis Lyamin para ser o novo chefe das novas Forças de Sistemas Não-Tripulados. Num "futuro próximo", o Presidente russo espera que esteja operacional.

observador.title: Menos telemóveis significa menos bullying?
observador.description: A proibição do uso de telemóveis vai ser alargada até ao 9.º ano. O psicólogo Eduardo Sá defende que a medida ajuda a proteger a saúde mental dos alunos.

observador.title: Teatros Variedades e Capitólio com mais de 40 espetáculos
observador.description: De setembro a dezembro, a EGEAC traz ópera, jazz, musicais e comédia a Lisboa. Temporada arranca a 2 de setembro no Variedades com a peça "Lote 19".

observador.title: Trovoadas no fim de semana, rios europeus secos e gafanhotos
observador.description: O tempo em Portugal continua instável, com calor até ao fim de semana e depois trovoadas e chuva. Pela Europa o calor secou os grandes ricos. E a Rússia enfrente uma praga de gafanhotos.

observador.title: Cabaz alimentar volta a subir para 253,60 euros
observador.description: Alho seco, fiambre e pão de forma lideram os aumentos semanais. Desde 2022, a carne de novilho para cozer disparou 120% e o bacalhau 89%.

observador.title: Acampamento contra a exploração de lítio na mina em Boticas
observador.description: A sexta edição do evento decorre de quinta a domingo em Covas do Barroso. As inscrições fecharam mais cedo devido ao elevado número de interessados.

observador.title: "Só o diálogo pode resolver" conflito EUA-Irão
observador.description: A embaixadora do Paquistão em Lisboa considerou a necessidade de entendimento entre os dois países como "um assunto global", reconhecendo a dor do povo iraniano, insistindo no diálogo como solução.

observador.title: Prestação da casa aumenta em Agosto
observador.description: A subida recente das taxas Euribor vai continuar a sentir-se na revisão de Agosto das prestações do crédito à habitação.

observador.title: 16h. Israel reivindica novos ataques no sul do Líbano
observador.description: Forças de Defesa Israelitas dizem ter levado a cabo "ataques precisos" na região em resposta a uma "violação flagrante do cessar-fogo" do Hezbollah. Ainda, S.C. Braga e FC Dinamo Minsk jogam amanhã.

observador.title: Preço das casas desacelera pelo oitavo mês consecutivo
observador.description: O preço por metro quadrado das casas continua a aumentar, mas aumento é cada vez menor. De acordo com dados do Idealista, o crescimento homólogo de preços em Julho foi de 8%. Em Novembro foi de 14,4%.

observador.title: Autoridades: apreenderam mais cocaína em 2026 do que em 2025
observador.description: As autoridades portuguesas já apreenderam 28 toneladas de cocaína desde o início de 2026, mais três do que em todo 2025. A última apreensão foi feita na terça-feira no Porto de Sines.

observador.title: Amadores de Música ainda à espera de espaço
observador.description: Passado um ano desde a luta por um novo espaço em Lisboa, mantém-se a espera pela cedência de um edifício na Avenida de Berna, disse à Lusa o presidente desta instituição histórica.

observador.title: Ponte 25 de Abril com espetáculo de drones sobre o Tejo
observador.description: Espetáculo será a partir da margem sul do rio e poderá ser visível a partir da zona das Docas, em Lisboa. Ministro Pinto Luz estará presente. Empresas evocam papel da "infraestrutura estratégica".

observador.title: Burnham não vai investigar ação de Epstein no Reino Unido
observador.description: Durante a campanha para a liderança dos trabalhistas, Burnham terá recebido um pedido pedia para investigar como Epstein viajou para bases militares britânicas no seu jato, com mulheres traficadas.

observador.title: Detido traficante e apreendida heroína e cocaína em Setúbal
observador.description: O homem "evidenciou um comportamento suspeito" ao ser abordado pelos militares. Após revista, a Guarda verificou que estava na posse das 226 doses de heroína e das 113 de cocaína.

observador.title: Código das Expropriações alterado entra em vigor
observador.description: Executivo foi autorizado pelo Parlamento a alterar. Programa do Governo "aprofunda a descentralização". Competências alargadas para "declaração de utilidade pública" pelas assembleias municipais.

elpais.title: La Audiencia Nacional pregunta a la Guardia Civil si tuvo alguna información que pudiese “alertar” de la entrada masiva en Ceuta
elpais.description: La instructora solicita también datos sobre los operativos de rescate y los fallecidos

elpais.title: Marruecos procesa a 77  personas por organizar cruces irregulares en Ceuta y Melilla
elpais.description: La justicia les imputa delitos relacionados con la salida clandestina del país, transporte de pasajeros sin licencia o agresiones a los miembros de las fuerzas de seguridad

elpais.title: Censos improvisados en el barrio de El Príncipe tras la llegada de cientos de menores: “Esto rompe cualquier parámetro”
elpais.description: En la periferia de la ciudad, los vecinos se hacen cargo de los menores migrantes que cruzaron a nado y que las autoridades no saben dónde ubicar

elpais.title: Playa de Trampolín: el refugio a sol abierto para centenares de subsaharianos que resisten en busca de asilo
elpais.description: Centenares de migrantes se agolpan en una pequeña cala de la ciudad, a la espera de un asilo que no llega

elpais.title: Ayuso dice que es la Consejería de Presidencia quien debe dar explicaciones sobre la compra del ático: “Yo no tengo la menor idea”
elpais.description: La presidenta de Madrid asegura que son los consejeros los responsables de este tipo de operaciones

elpais.title: Dos pacientes extranjeros atrapados en Urgencias. “Esta es la prioridad nacional aplicada a un hospital”
elpais.description: Un señor boliviano con un tumor incurable pasa casi una semana en la unidad sin ser trasladado a planta en el hospital Puerta de Hierro, y un chico de origen peruano lleva 14 días. Los trabajadores creen que la dirección ahorra costes con inmigrantes sin familia que no van a presentar una queja

elpais.title: Dime cómo es tu siesta y te diré cómo estás de salud: lo que algunas cabezadas revelan sobre el envejecimiento
elpais.description: El tiempo total de sueño va disminuyendo de forma lineal según envejecemos. Los médicos consideran los reposos matutinos prolongados una señal negativa

elpais.title: “Le tenía que haber dado más fuerte”: Éric Cantona, el futbolista que convirtió una patada a un racista en un evento social
elpais.description: El futbolista reconvertido en actor sigue en activo en la pantalla con un documental sobre su vida, una comedia como protagonista y la serie ‘El viajero’, que acaba de estrenar en Cosmo

elpais.title: El día que Clint Eastwood le dio una lección de humildad a Kevin Costner en el set de ‘Un mundo perfecto’
elpais.description: En 1993, el director, conocido por hacer rodajes rápidos y grabar las escenas en pocas tomas, reemplazó al actor con su doble por hacerle esperar con las cámaras preparadas

elpais.title: El reto del pantalón corto masculino
elpais.description: Pocas cosas despiertan más inseguridades entre los hombres que cambiar la longitud del pantalón y el significado de enseñar más o menos pierna.

elpais.title: Penélope Cruz y Salma Hayek: la anécdota del maquillaje como prueba de una de las amistades más sólidas de Hollywood
elpais.description: La española ha comentado que una entrevista reciente que su amistad es tan cercana que incluso la ha peinado y maquillado cuando ha fallado el equipo de Salma. Un ‘brochazo’ más sobre una amistad de más de 20 años

elpais.title: ¿Cómo y dónde conseguir gratis las gafas homologadas para ver el eclipse total de agosto?
elpais.description: La ONCE y el Gobierno reparten dos millones de unidades. Muchos establecimientos las regalan: así se comprueba que están homologadas

elpais.title: Consejos para disfrutar del eclipse: “Ni siquiera uno del 99,99% tiene nada que ver con las sensaciones de uno total”
elpais.description: La totalidad apenas durará unos minutos, por lo que se recomienda situarse dentro de la franja, utilizar gafas homologadas y evitar que hacer fotografías reste protagonismo a la experiencia

elpais.title: La policía alemana desactiva un dron bomba que cayó junto a un avión de carga ucranio en el aeropuerto de Leipzig
elpais.description: Un segundo aparato no tripulado ha impactado con una aeronave de carga que volaba en las inmediaciones del aeropuerto de Leipzig

elpais.title: El verdulero ‘cazado’ por un dron en Ucrania: “Le enseñé que solo tenía verduras, pero empezó a volar hacia mí”
elpais.description: El hombre, de 52 años, identificado como Yurii, sufrió heridas por metralla y una conmoción cerebral. Zelenski describió el episodio como ejemplo de “safari humano”

elpais.title: Ola de indignación en Perú por una agresión sexual contra una cantante de cumbia
elpais.description: Los videos en los que la intérprete Naldy Saldaña aparece siendo sometida a tocamientos por el director musical de la orquesta La Bella Luz han escandalizado a la población peruana. La Fiscalía investiga el caso

elpais.title: El progresista Abdul El-Sayed gana las primarias demócratas en Míchigan, una batalla clave para el futuro del partido
elpais.description: El aspirante a senador, muy crítico con Israel y defensor de la sanidad pública universal, logra una victoria muy ajustada tras 13 horas de conteo

elpais.title: Las 19 quejas de Bolaños sobre Peinado que el CGPJ archivó: “Censuró mi expresión facial y me prohibió sonreír”
elpais.description: El ministro escribió cinco cartas a Perelló denunciando peticiones “atípicas” y comentarios “intimidatorios” del juez cuando le interrogó como testigo

nyt.title: Shri Thanedar Is Ousted by a Democratic Socialist in a Michigan House Primary
nyt.description: Representative Shri Thanedar is among a wave of Democratic incumbents in Congress whom primary voters have sent packing in a surge of anti-incumbent fervor this cycle.

nyt.title: Takeaways From the Primary Elections in Michigan
nyt.description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed narrowly prevailed over Representative Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary for Senate in Michigan, setting up a nervy race to November for the party.

nyt.title: Rep. Chuck Edwards Drops Re-election Bid in North Carolina After Ethics Rebuke
nyt.description: Chuck Edwards made the announcement after the House Ethics Committee recommended he be censured for “persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct” toward two female staff members.

nyt.title: How the Ukraine War Became a Fight for the Skies
nyt.description: Russia and Ukraine are producing ever larger numbers of innovative aerial weapons, hoping for a breakthrough as ground combat is largely frozen.

nyt.title: Russia’s Deadly Missile Attack on Kyiv Exploits Ukraine’s Depleted Air Defenses
nyt.description: At least 17 people were killed, officials said, as the country runs desperately low on interceptor missiles that could fend off Russian bombardments.

nyt.title: The U.S. Relies on Family Caregivers. Millions of Them Are Kids.
nyt.description: The modern health care system requires the work of caregiving to fall to whoever else lives in a household — even if they’re kids.

nyt.title: Israeli Strikes May Undermine Trump’s Peace Plan for Gaza
nyt.description: President Trump announced a proposal aimed at achieving the disarmament of Hamas and an Israeli withdrawal. Israel ramped up attacks on the Palestinian enclave.

nyt.title: Israel Strikes Lebanon After Accusing Hezbollah of Cease-Fire Violation
nyt.description: At the same time, Israeli and Lebanese negotiators were holding talks in Rome aimed at fostering a long-term diplomatic settlement.

nyt.title: Houthis Threaten to Expand Red Sea Attacks, and Claim Strike on Saudi Tanker
nyt.description: Saudi Arabia has not commented on the claim by the Houthis, who are backed by Iran and have vowed to close “all access routes” to Saudi oil shipments.

nyt.title: They Were Voted Out. They Refuse to Leave. Now What?
nyt.description: Avenal, Calif., a city in the rural Central Valley, has become an unlikely example of election denialism months after a recall election.

nyt.title: Migrant Crisis Reveals Vast Differences Between Ceuta and Its Moroccan Neighbor
nyt.description: Ceuta, Spain, and Fnideq, Morocco, are physically separated by only a mile, but they are intertwined by family and trade. A recent border crisis is the latest chapter in their story.

nyt.title: What One Witness Saw Before a Spokane Wildfire Started
nyt.description: A resident of Spokane County, Wash., said he noticed a man acting suspiciously and called 911 after seeing smoke. The police later arrested a suspect tied to one of the wildfires in the area.

nyt.title: Climate Change Comes to Sesame Street
nyt.description: An episode this week focuses on the dangerous effects of warming, without mentioning climate change.

nyt.title: He Had Tenure. The New School Laid Him Off Anyway.
nyt.description: The professor, a longtime critic of the university, was among 19 educators who lost their positions as the institution navigated financial woes.

nyt.title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Draws Fans to Richmond, a Picturesque London Suburb
nyt.description: Fans of the warmhearted Apple TV show flock to Richmond-upon-Thames, which has long been a destination for visitors and film location scouts.

nyt.title: On ‘Ted Lasso,’ Hannah Waddingham Is Ruthless. Off Camera, She’s ‘Quite a Goofy Nugget.’
nyt.description: Hannah Waddingham is a rare British actor to beat a path from musical theater to the screen.

nyt.title: The Tradwife Illusion Meets the Anti-Trump Reality
nyt.description: Nara Smith’s illusion meets the anti-Trump reality.

nyt.title: Lessons on the Way to 100
nyt.description: We want to hear from people who aspire to live long lives — maybe even to 100 or beyond — about how you hope to do it and, perhaps, how you have been inspired by others who have made it there.

npr.title: Under China's new 'unity' law, Tibetans fight to preserve language and culture
npr.description: A 73-year-old retired nurse's decision to learn to write Tibetan language offers a glimpse into how some embrace their language and cultural identity in Tibet.

npr.title: U.S. missile stockpiles dwindle. And, FDA weighs approval of flu shots with mRNA tech
npr.description: The U.S. Army's missile stockpile is dwindling and could take years to replenish. And, the Food and Drug Administration is deciding whether to approve a flu vaccine with mRNA technology.

npr.title: Russian missile and drone barrage in Ukrainian capital region kills 17
npr.description: Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region killed 17 people and wounded 44 others overnight into Wednesday, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

npr.title: Unrest mounts in Kashmir as Pakistani security crackdown stokes reform movement
npr.description: Pakistani forces blockade Kashmir as protesters demand electoral reforms and -- increasingly -- revolution.

npr.title: Ukraine's air defenses are proving to be a weak point
npr.description: Ukraine's defenses have held the line on most fronts, but there's one glaring weakness -- Russian ballistic missiles. Ukraine is desperately short of U.S.-made Patriot air defense missiles needed to defend against the Russians.

npr.title: The soaring demand for Patriot missiles, from the Middle East to Ukraine
npr.description: The U.S. and its partners depend on Patriot interceptors to shoot down incoming ballistic missiles. But Russia and Iran are firing their weapons at rates far higher than Patriots can be produced.

npr.title: Europe's heat wave fuels drought, wildfires and fears about energy supplies
npr.description: Europe's heat wave exposes buried history and new threats — Nazi-era wrecks emerge from the Danube, nuclear reactors face cooling risks, and Greece battles deadly wildfires.

npr.title: Nauru, the world's 3rd-smallest country, changes its name to Naoero
npr.description: The Pacific Island country of Nauru has changed its name to the Republic of Naoero, its president said, matching the spelling and pronunciation in the national language.

npr.title: With U.S. doors shutting, Cubans turn to Brazil for asylum
npr.description: For years, many Cubans hoping to leave the island looked to the United States. Now, with legal pathways largely closed, a growing number are heading to Brazil instead.

npr.title: Todd Blanche rescinds 'anti-weaponization fund'. And, Trump calls off striking Iran
npr.description: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche rescinds President Trump's anti-weaponization fund ahead of his confirmation hearing. And, the president calls off strikes on Iran over a potential deal.

republika.title: In aula torna il cappio (33 anni dopo), ma stavolta è agitato contro la Lega
republika.description: Il deputato di Futuro nazionale Edoardo Ziello esibisce la corda bianca all’indirizzo del ministro Giorgetti, accusato di strozzare l’economia italiana. Era accaduto nel 1993 al tramonto della Prima Repubblica: allora l’iniziativa del parlamentare del Carroccio Leoni

republika.title: Caso Delmastro, oggi il voto in aula sulle chat. Deputati di Avs bendati per protesta
republika.description: La seduta alla Camera dopo la decisione presa in giunta per le autorizzazioni. Attesi gli interventi di Schlein e Conte

republika.title: Porta inviolata e un gran gol di Zhegrova, la Juve batte il Chelsea a Hong Kong
republika.description: Buona prova della squadra di Spalletti, decide un sinistro a giro del kosovaro

republika.title: Taddeucci fa il bis, oro anche nella 5 km di fondo agli Europei. Bronzo a Pozzobon
republika.description: L’azzurra si ripete dopo il successo nella 10 km

republika.title: Milan-Inter a Perth, il ricordo di Baresi: rossoneri in campo con la maglia numero 6
republika.description: Prima dell’amichevole in Australia è stato ricordato lo storico capitano scomparso di recente

republika.title: L’italiano finito nei tg spagnoli: “Io, fermato a Fiumicino dopo Ceuta. Controlli senza senso”
republika.description: Intervista a Leandro Tirreno, makeup artist che da 12 anni si è trasferito a Barcellona: madre filippina, padre italiano, tratti somatici orientaleggianti, sabato scorso è stato uno dei primi bloccati dalla polizia in aeroporto dopo la sospensione di Schengen. Ed è diventato un servizio televisivo

republika.title: Georgina Rodriguez: “Mi dicono grassa”. Ronaldo: “Normale”. Il corpo delle donne sempre sotto esame
republika.description: Troppo magra, troppo formosa, cambiata, invecchiata: per il corpo femminile sembra non esistere mai una versione ‘giusta’. I casi di Georgina e di Ariana Grande sono solo gli ultimi di una lunga serie: perché continuiamo a sentirci autorizzati a giudicare corpi che non ci appartengono?

republika.title: Dal Piemonte all’Abruzzo, stelle cadenti e desideri nei Borghi più belli
republika.description: Torna l’iniziativa “Il Borgo dei Desideri”, promossa dall'associazione I Borghi più belli d'Italia per la notte di San Lorenzo

republika.title: Maturità, aumentano le lodi e calano i 100: le contraddizioni con i test Invalsi tra nord e sud
republika.description: Sono stati ammessi all’Esame di Stato il 96,7% dei candidati, mentre quasi tutti hanno poi conseguito il diploma. Crescono ancora le lodi, soprattutto nei licei e nelle regioni del Sud, mentre diminuiscono i 100 pieni

republika.title: Spese militari, il Pd si divide sulla risoluzione unitaria. Ma il voto salta grazie al regolamento
republika.description: Il testo di dem, Avs e M5S chiedeva di non usare lo scostamento per la difesa ma per povertà e crisi energetica. I riformisti del partito: “Non l’avremmo sostenuto”. E si esprimono a favore del Safe con Italia viva e +Europa.

republika.title: Aeroporto di Lipsia, tornano i droni: uno con esplosivo vicino a cargo di Kiev, l’altro urta volo
republika.description: Secondo indiscrezioni, alle indagini starebbero partecipando anche inquirenti della Nato

republika.title: Eclissi di sole, un borgo della Castiglia vedrà il tramonto due volte
republika.description: L’attesa per l’evento, il primo oscuramento totale in Europa da 27 anni a questa parte. In Spagna, dove l’ultimo episodio risale al 1912, il cono della totalità scivolerà dalla costa atlantica sino alle Baleari. Ma in un piccolo villaggio del nord del Paese, la congiuntura sarà assai particolare: si potranno ammirare due golden hour e due notti, una appresso all’altra

republika.title: Molina alla Roma, è fatta. Ora è caccia a Nusa, ma il Lipsia vuole 60 milioni
republika.description: Accordo con l’Atletico Madrid per l’esterno argentino. Si tratta con il Lipsia per il norvegese

republika.title: Banche russe a corto di liquidità. Così si chiudono per Mosca i rubinetti che finanziano la guerra

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

phys-org.description: New University of Georgia research suggests that social media could influence people's travel plans. The paper is published in the journal Current Issues in Tourism.

phys-org.title: Astronomers catch massive star's death from the first explosive moment
phys-org.description: In March 2026, the Einstein Probe detected a brief flash of soft X-rays emitted from a galaxy about 500 million light-years away. The flash, dubbed EP260321a, immediately triggered a worldwide observing campaign. Within an hour, ground-based telescopes began monitoring the source, revealing a rapidly brightening supernova, later designated SN 2026gzf. Two teams of scientists used several NSF NOIRLab facilities to observe the event and monitor its evolving light profile.

phys-org.title: SpaceX rocket stage believed to have slammed into the moon
phys-org.description: A piece of a SpaceX rocket weighing four tonnes (4.4 tons) was believed to have unintentionally crashed into the moon on Wednesday, a collision that posed no danger to Earth but is expected to leave behind a lunar crater.

phys-org.title: Gene-edited beagles may offer a future option for people with dog allergies
phys-org.description: Matt Walker couldn't pet a dog without sneezing—until he and other scientists used a gene editing technique to produce a hypoallergenic beagle named Bailey.

phys-org.title: Human activity more than doubles Arctic fire occurrence, satellite analysis suggests
phys-org.description: Fires in the Arctic are not solely a regional issue, as shown by the hazy skies in Switzerland last summer despite otherwise sunny weather. Smoke from major fires in northern Canada crossed the Atlantic and reached Europe. Until now, large-scale studies of Arctic tundra fires have focused primarily on rising temperatures and drought as the main drivers. The role of human activity has received much less attention, even as industrial development, settlements, roads and other infrastructure expand

phys-org.title: Avalanche cracks may appear globally supersonic while remaining locally subsonic
phys-org.description: Can a crack be supersonic? Can the fracture that triggers an avalanche propagate faster than the limiting velocity predicted by classical fracture mechanics? The question remains the subject of debate within the scientific community. While some numerical and experimental studies suggest that avalanche cracks may propagate at supersonic speeds, others offer a different interpretation.

phys-org.title: Pumas make roads safer for drivers by changing prey behavior patterns
phys-org.description: Living among large predatory carnivores could actually make you safer. A study published in the journal Current Biology found that pumas—wild cats also known as mountain lions, cougars or panthers—change deer behavior, leading to fewer collisions with cars on roadways. In areas where puma occupancy is high, the authors report a significant reduction in the total expected number of collisions over a 5-year period.

phys-org.title: Turning one of the world's most difficult plastics into premium lubricant
phys-org.description: Virginia Tech chemist and chemical engineer Guoliang "Greg" Liu and his lab have developed a process that converts the plastic polyvinyl chloride (PVC) into polyalphaolefin, a key component in lubricants such as engine oil. Published Aug. 5 in the journal Nature, the research could help address two environmental challenges: recycling one of the world's most difficult plastics and producing a valuable industrial material.

phys-org.description: Researchers from the U.S. National Science Foundation National Solar Observatory (NSF NSO), the Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS) in Germany, and the High Altitude Observatory (HAO) in the U.S. have made a discovery in solar physics. New images of the sun's surface taken with the world's largest solar telescope, the NSF Daniel K. phys-org.title: Act now on microplastic risks, businesses urged
phys-org.description: A new white paper released by experts at the UTS Business School highlights the risks businesses face if they ignore growing scientific evidence and consumer awareness of the dangers posed by microplastics.

phys-org.title: Backpack lab finds wastewater contamination and drug-resistant bacteria in Galápagos waters
phys-org.description: From routine surgeries to cancer treatment, modern medicine depends on drugs that can fight infections caused by microbes such as bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites. But some microbes are becoming resistant to the drugs used to treat them, which has wide-reaching consequences for global public health.

phys-org.title: Ancient armored fish that narrowly avoided meteorite strike reveals life before Earth's largest mass extinction
phys-org.description: A rare fossil discovered near South America's largest known meteorite crater has been named a new species. Initially mistaken for a frog by locals, Leolepis matogrossensis is actually a species of ancient ray-finned fish—the group that includes 96% of all bony fishes living today, including tuna, salmon and cod. It's a fairly primitive member of the group and lived around 254 million years ago.

phys-org.title: Noisy bubbles hinder ultrasound-boosted chemical reactions, sonochemistry model shows
phys-org.description: Ultrasound is a powerful way to drive chemical reactions. When high-frequency sound waves pass through a liquid, tiny bubbles form and then violently collapse in a process called acoustic cavitation. During this collapse, gas particles are forced together, creating temperatures inside the bubbles that can exceed 5,000 K—hotter than the surface of the sun—and driving chemical reactions.

phys-org.title: Soilless farming system design can determine microbial growth, impact on crops
phys-org.description: Soilless farming—a method of growing plants in a nutrient-rich solution rather than traditional soil—accounts for a significant share of vegetable production, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), with more than half of tomatoes, cucumbers and lettuce grown using hydroponics. This fast-growing segment of modern agriculture addresses water scarcity, land limitations and food security, but microbial management remains a challenge, according to a team of researchers at Penn State.

phys-org.title: Were there tiny dinosaurs? New study explores one of evolution's biggest mysteries
phys-org.description: Dinosaurs are famous for being big, from the towering Tyrannosaurus rex to the colossal Apatosaurus. But a new study published today in the journal Evolution by scientists at the American Museum of Natural History and Princeton University suggests that one of the greatest mysteries of dinosaur evolution isn't how some species became giants—it's why even the smallest dinosaurs never became truly tiny.

phys-org.title: A new take on interpreting chemical bond analysis in solids
phys-org.description: Researchers from Skoltech, SberUniversity, the M.N. Mikheev Institute of Metal Physics of UB RAS and Ural Federal University have published a review of a novel approach to interpreting chemical bonding in solids. The method not only describes crystals in terms of precise calculations but also enables chemists to reclaim explanatory models that are intuitively meaningful to them. The insights that emerge span long-documented anomalies that previously lacked a theoretical account.

phys-org.title: Study finds climate-driven greening is reshaping East Asia's air pollution
phys-org.description: The effects of climate change extend far beyond rising temperatures. As forests and other vegetation respond to a warming world, they also change the amount of biogenic emissions released into the atmosphere, influencing the formation of ozone (O3) and fine particulate pollution. Yet many atmospheric chemistry models still estimate these emissions using vegetation data from 2003, despite major ecological changes across East Asia over the past two decades.

phys-org.title: Study suggests natural sounds help us feel more attached to specific places
phys-org.description: A new study suggests the sounds around us have a significant impact on how we feel about physical spaces, with natural sounds—such as birdsong—associated with a greater sense of attachment to a given place. The study draws on data from a large-scale participatory science project involving more than 1,000 citizen scientists.

proj-syn.title: Aid’s Next Chapter
proj-syn.description: Wars, epidemics, displacement, and geopolitical competition will ensure that rich countries continue to spend money abroad, whether for humanitarian reasons or in pursuit of their own interests. The only question is what sort of aid system will emerge from the current retrenchment.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Won’t Last Unless It Benefits Ordinary Iranians
proj-syn.description: A sustainable peace agreement between the United States and Iran will require more than military deterrence. Without financial sanctions relief that fuels job creation and generates real economic opportunities for ordinary Iranians, it will likely suffer the same fate as the 2015 nuclear deal.

proj-syn.title: Why Wealth Taxes Always Fail
proj-syn.description: A clear-eyed view of past experience shows that where wealth taxes have been tried, they have usually been abandoned—and for good reason. As policymakers in California, New York, France, and elsewhere revisit this old idea, they should heed the lessons of this history.

proj-syn.title: A New Paradigm for Global Health Financing
proj-syn.description: As aid flows decline, more countries are articulating a new vision in which health financing would build on national resources, answer to domestic priorities, and remain accountable to their own citizens. Such a change is long overdue, and it can be achieved by pursuing reforms in three areas.

proj-syn.title: The Triumph of India’s Cockroaches
proj-syn.description: The concessions secured by the "cockroach movement" amount to more than a triumph for prospective medical students or a brief political headache for the country's ruling party. They prove that even after years of centralization and institutional erosion, power remains with the people.

proj-syn.title: Zombie Monetarism
proj-syn.description: Three prominent economists, including a former Federal Reserve governor and adviser to US President Donald Trump, have just endorsed “soft monetarism” as a way to guide the Fed's approach to inflation. But the "quantity theory" of money failed for good reasons, and those reasons have not changed.

proj-syn.title: Taiwan Needs a New Deterrence Strategy
proj-syn.description: Emboldened by US President Donald Trump’s war in Iran, Chinese leaders have ramped up their gray-zone coercion against Taiwan in recent months. To avert a Chinese invasion, Taiwan must ensure that other democracies cannot function without it by providing them with more than just semiconductors.

proj-syn.title: What a Sino-American G2 Would Mean for Asian Security
proj-syn.description: The G2 concept that Donald Trump has lately been touting is a highly unstable proposition, which could make the emergence of a unipolar Asia more likely. Fortunately, Japan remains committed to advancing the far more effective “free and open Indo-Pacific” framework, with India as an indispensable partner.

proj-syn.title: Tearing Down the Currency Wall
proj-syn.description: Most of the world seems to misunderstand why global capital is not financing the developing world’s climate transition. The real problem lies in the structure of price formation, which policymakers can best address by focusing on three key priorities.

proj-syn.title: The Case for a Pay-Where-You-Play Tax System
proj-syn.description: The global tax system has repeatedly put corporate interests ahead of people and the planet by allowing multinationals to transfer profits to tax havens. If adopted, the proposed UN Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation would overturn the century-old rules that make this possible.

proj-syn.title: The Canary in the AI Coal Mine
proj-syn.description: The greatest danger posed by AI is not the technology itself, but the race to deploy it before we know how to control it. The recent Hugging Face breach shows how seemingly minor human errors can be amplified by AI, underscoring the risks of treating safety as an afterthought.

proj-syn.title: The Painful Incompetence of the Indian State
proj-syn.description: India’s relatively weak state capacity has long hampered its development. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been promising to address the problem since he came to power in 2014, but his government’s emphasis on centralizing power and strengthening executive control has had the opposite effect.

proj-syn.title: This Time Could Be Different for Russia Sanctions
proj-syn.description: High inflation and interest rates are eating away at the foundations of the Russian economy and sapping its growth. By hitting its most important sectors, and its essential source of foreign hard cash, new US legislation would pile enormous pressure on the Kremlin just when it is urgently needed.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s Energy Curse Is a Political Choice
proj-syn.description: It is no secret why African countries with large fossil-fuel reserves nonetheless have failed to reduce extreme poverty or provide reliable electricity to all households. Those in power have made a conscious choice to privilege hard-currency export revenues, some of which then finance elite consumption rather than public investment.

proj-syn.title: The EU’s Incredible Shrinking Banking Sector
proj-syn.description: At the start of the millennium, all five of the largest European banks had a higher market capitalization than the largest US bank. What explains the fact that a quarter-century later, the largest US bank has a higher capitalization than all five top EU banks combined, and how can European policymakers address this dramatic reversal?

proj-syn.title: AI Must Enlarge the Economy, Not Divide It
proj-syn.description: To unlock AI’s full economic potential, we must steer it toward expansion. That requires replacing incentives that favor capital over labor with those that reward augmentation and investment in human capability.

proj-syn.title: Silicon, Not Software, Will Decide the AI Race
proj-syn.description: The AI race is no longer just about building better models. As competition shifts from scientific discovery to deployment, success increasingly depends on computing power, advanced semiconductors, physical infrastructure, and markets large enough to justify the enormous investments they require.

proj-syn.title: The Limits of Asia’s Two Major Growth Models
proj-syn.description: Data from a period in which both China and India pursued deliberate industrial policies show that neither country's development route is accessible to other countries. At best, their experience can alert policymakers to structural limitations and coordination problems that will require their own homegrown solutions.
